question: What evidence is required to compare our Signaling / Non-signaling Tester solution with a competitor for Wireless Communication without making unsupported claims?
answer: For a signaling / non-signaling tester comparison (R&S CMX500 / CMW500 on the signaling side, CMP180 / CMP200 / CMW100 K06 on the non-signaling production side) the Vault requires evidence at three layers. First, R&S capability claims must be traced to the formal documents — CMX500_specs_en_5216-4127-22_v1100, CMX500_Features_CSW9-20-0_en_32, CMW_dat-sw_en_5213-9211-22_v1700 — and each production / non-signaling platform must be cited from its own official source page; the competitive synthesis pages explicitly cannot replace them. Second, the 2026-02-26 sales battle cards (Keysight / Anritsu / amarisoft) are sales positioning, not binding technical specifications, so their numbers (FR1 500 MHz or 18 GHz, RFU18 2000 MHz aggregated bandwidth, >16 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, >10 Gbps) may only be quoted as a dated sales claim and must never be back-filled into CMX500 specifications. Third, every competitor statement currently rests on a single R&S internal battle card, so customer-facing use requires the competitor's own official data plus third-party evidence; conversely a competitor's official brochure (e.g. mx844030pc-j1200 for the Anritsu MX844030PC Virtual Signalling Tester) may describe that competitor's product but cannot validate an R&S advantage claim. Superlatives — "only platform", "first validated", "industry-leading", "widest frequency range", "lower TCO", "fewer boxes" — are sales language and are not usable as verifiable specifications; TCO in particular has no formula or supporting data in the sources. Validated-conformance and NTN claims additionally need a validation report, test case list and PTCRB RFT version/date, and demo-level PR sources need bandwidth, throughput, MCS, MIMO configuration and measurement uncertainty before being treated as capability evidence.
missing: The Vault has no page using the exact category label "Signaling / Non-signaling Tester" or a "Wireless Communication" solution taxonomy, and no single consolidated evidence-policy page; the rules above are assembled from the three competitive synthesis pages, the battle card source notes and the FR3/RFU18 concept page. Also missing in the Vault: Keysight / Anritsu / amarisoft official datasheets and order data, the RFU18 formal specification, and any TCO calculation or third-party benchmark.
